title: Dorm university student (no job, 4 classes, 12 credits, online Physics, Canvas, afternoon steady) eats out $7.07 a week more than usual this month; nothing is due, so there is no fix and Dev says nothing at 4 PM on Thursday, and no study on his kept-free Sunday morning.

best_fix.what: Nothing. At 4:00 PM on Thursday Nov 12 the Tonight card shows that the evening is open (no class, no study window pending, dinner on his meal plan) and nothing else. No spending card: eating out is $31.88 a week this month against $24.81 before (about $7.07 more), Available now is $1,745.26, savings are $350.37, the only bills are small subscriptions (the next is Spotify $5.99 on Dec 3), and he has no income to protect. A figure with no fix attached is not worth his attention.
best_fix.why: Spending above usual is only worth saying when Dev has a fix, such as a bill at risk, a goal falling behind, or a charge that is wrong. Here nothing is at risk, so any message would be a scolding.

must_not: send a spending-above-usual message about eating out
suggest cooking, skipping meals or cutting the meal plan
count a refund, aid or family money that has not landed
put a study block on Sunday morning

tempting.suggestion: put a study block on Sunday morning
tempting.why_wrong: Sunday 8 AM to noon is his fixed kept-free time; he studies weekday afternoons from 2:00 to 4:45

assumptions: Eating out of $24.81 a week before and $31.88 a week during is the simulator's measured effect, over Nov 2 to Nov 12.
The meal plan covers 14 dining hall meals a week, so some of the extra is a choice, not a need.
The family call Sunday evening and the kept-free morning are both untouched.
